NEWS: Kazakhstan is planning to expand the use of Tesla Cybertrucks in emergency response operations ⚡

The move comes after officials reported encouraging results from the country's first Cybertruck deployment in rescue and emergency service missions.

As more organizations test the vehicle in real-world conditions, the Cybertruck is increasingly being viewed as more than just a consumer pickup.

UPDATE: Tesla is offering discounts on inventory Model 3 vehicles across the U.S.

Multiple new and demo units are currently listed with price reductions of up to $1,700, with some vehicles also including 1 year of free Supercharging.

The deals bring several Model 3 variants into the low-$40,000 range, making Tesla's best-selling sedan even more competitive.

BREAKING: Tesla just had its best month ever in Australia.

Tesla delivered 6,433 vehicles in May 2026, setting a new all-time monthly sales record and surpassing the previous high of 6,017 vehicles set in March 2024.

The Model Y led the charge with 5,605 deliveries, accounting for 84% of Tesla's total sales for the month and securing its position as Australia's best-selling EV.

Tesla says a key driver behind the momentum is the six-seat Model Y L.

Starting at $74,900 plus on-road costs, it's currently the only six-seat battery-electric vehicle available in Australia and is proving especially popular with families and fleet buyers.

The numbers show Tesla's demand remains strong as the company continues expanding its presence across the Australian market.

BREAKING: Tesla China just posted its strongest sales growth of 2026.

May sales surged 39.44% year-over-year, marking a major rebound for Tesla in the world's largest EV market.

The result comes as Tesla continues ramping production at Gigafactory Shanghai while demand for the refreshed Model Y gains momentum across China.

Shanghai remains one of Tesla's most important manufacturing hubs and this latest jump shows the company is still competing at a very high level in an increasingly crowded EV market.
